learning_outcomes: Explain what environment variables and secret management contributes to a PHP application.

content.intro: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. In this lesson, focus on environment configuration; then compare it with api keys and database credentials. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use environment variables and secret management when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. For environment variables and secret management, begin with environment configuration. Also distinguish api keys and database credentials; secret files and access permissions; secret rotation. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Environment configuration
items.text: Know when to use environment configuration, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: API keys and database credentials
items.text: Keep query structure separate from data values, check failures explicitly, and use constraints or transactions when integrity depends on multiple operations.

items.title: Secret files and access permissions
items.text: Distinguish identity verification from resource permission, and test expiry, invalid credentials, and denied access as well as the success path.

items.title: Secret rotation
items.text: Treat the relevant value as untrusted, apply the defense at the correct boundary, and verify a deliberately invalid or hostile-looking input is rejected or encoded.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.
